# Glyphfield agent operating guide

Glyphfield is a local-first brand system, visual Studio, deterministic generation API, and authentic browser-rendering surface. This file is the concise router. Load `/llms-full.txt` when the task needs the complete documentation corpus.

## Start here

1. Read `GET /api/agent` for the current manifest, policies, interfaces, execution rules, and generation schema.
2. Read `GET /api/labs` for the live Studio tool list. Never hard-code its count.
3. Read the task-specific catalog: `/api/materials`, `/api/identities`, `/api/elements`, or `/api/catalog`.
4. Read `GET /api/generate` immediately before constructing a generation request.
5. Choose HTTP or the Browser API according to the artifact, then verify the terminal result.

Machine-readable resources:

- Complete docs: `/llms-full.txt`
- One processed Markdown page: `/api/docs/{slug}`
- Human docs: `/docs`
- Search: `/api/search`
- OpenAPI: `/openapi.json`
- Agent manifest: `/api/agent`
- Studio catalog: `/api/labs`
- Full combined catalog: `/api/catalog`
- Shader catalog: `/api/materials`
- Allowlisted surface maps: `/api/surface-textures/:assetId/:map`
- Identity catalog: `/api/identities`
- Brand-element catalog: `/api/elements`
- Generation contract: `/api/generate`
- Interactive workspace: `/studio`
- Installable skill guide: `/docs/skills.md`

Repository Agent Skills:

- `skills/glyphfield-create`: layered Design Lab composition and saved-design work.
- `skills/glyphfield-api`: deterministic HTTP discovery and generation.
- `skills/glyphfield-studio`: live Studio controls, source round trips, files, and browser rendering.
- `skills/glyphfield-export`: artifact export and still/motion verification.

Load only the skill whose description matches the current task. Combine them when a workflow actually crosses generation, browser operation, and export boundaries.

## Choose the interface

Use `POST /api/generate` for deterministic SVG, structured element briefs, and apply-ready Design Lab source documents. It is appropriate for repeatable batch generation and source-controlled outputs.

Use `window.glyphfield.studio` inside `/studio` for anything that depends on the real browser workspace: Canvas, WebGL shaders, local files, local fonts, Lottie, direct visual placement, saved composition state, PNG, JPG, GIF, or MP4. This is not a fallback API; it is the programmatic interface to the authentic UI renderer.

Use both for a Design Lab sequence: create the versioned source with `kind: "design-sequence"`, apply `response.document` in the browser, then export through `design.export`.

Do not imitate a browser-rendered result with server SVG when the user requested the authentic live material, motion, font, or layout.

## HTTP generation

`POST /api/generate` accepts `Content-Type: application/json` and one of these `kind` values:

- `background`: deterministic SVG gradient, pattern, dither, or tactile surface; output `json` or `raw`.
- `template`: deterministic slide, blog-cover, or partnership SVG; output `json` or `raw`.
- `element-brief`: one brand-element brief resolved against a built-in or custom identity.
- `design-sequence`: a response-schema-1 envelope containing an apply-ready Design Lab version-3 compatibility document, resolved shader timeline, and browser commands. Applying it normalizes the active Studio source to CanvasDocument schema 2 with Design Lab source 4.

Unknown top-level fields are rejected. Treat structured `400`, `413`, `415`, and `429` responses as actionable errors. Do not retry unchanged invalid input.

Remote URL fetching is not supported. Provide authorized local data through allowed data-URL fields or a real browser `File` object.

## Studio Browser API

The active Studio tool registers `window.glyphfield.studio` and dispatches `glyphfield:studio-api-ready`. Re-read the global after changing tools because each tool installs its own adapter.

Core methods:

- `activeTool()` returns the public Studio tool ID. Design Lab is `material`; `logo-shader` is an internal legacy draft scope and must not be expected by integrations.
- `describe()` returns version, tool ID, source support, and exact action names.
- `controls()` lists accessible control labels, control kinds, and current values.
- `activate(label)` clicks a control by its exact accessible label.
- `set(label, value)` changes a supported input, select, checkbox, contenteditable, or file input.
- `readSource()` returns the active tool's complete source string.
- `applySource(source)` validates and applies an object or JSON string, then waits for the React commit boundary.
- `invoke(action, input?)` runs a standard or tool-specific action.
- `download({ blob, fileName })` saves a previously returned artifact.

Standard `invoke` actions are `source.read`, `source.apply`, `controls.list`, `control.activate`, `control.set`, and `artifact.download`.

Always call `describe()` before a tool-specific action. Never invent accessible labels or action names.

### Design Lab actions

Design Lab exposes:

```text
design.sequence.describe
design.sequence.configure
design.sequence.preview
design.sequence.stop
design.export
design.export.png
design.export.jpg
design.export.gif
design.export.mp4
design.export.shader-sequence.gif
design.export.shader-sequence.mp4
```

Preferred export call:

```js
const studio = window.glyphfield.studio;
if (studio.activeTool() !== 'material') throw new Error('Open Design Lab first.');

const artifact = await studio.invoke('design.export', {
  format: 'mp4',
  mode: 'shader-sequence',
  download: false,
});

if (!(artifact.blob instanceof Blob) || artifact.blob.size === 0) {
  throw new Error('The export is empty.');
}

studio.download(artifact);
```

`format` accepts `png`, `jpg`, `gif`, and `mp4`. `mode: "shader-sequence"` is valid for GIF and MP4. Run exports serially because browser canvases and encoders are shared resources.

## Source mutation protocol

1. Call `describe()` and confirm source read/apply support.
2. Call `readSource()` and parse the current document.
3. Preserve every unknown field. Make the smallest targeted change.
4. Call `applySource(document)`; never write React state, IndexedDB, or localStorage directly.
5. Re-read source and confirm the intended value round-tripped.
6. Inspect the rendered canvas when the requested result is visual.
7. Export only after the preview is ready.

Design Lab's active source is a versioned CanvasDocument. It contains assets, capabilities, elements, pages, layer order, transforms, styles, opacity, blend modes, text and converter effects, shaders, saved sequence settings, and export settings. Do not rebuild this envelope from memory. For an existing design, start from `readSource()`. For a new generated sequence, apply the version-3 compatibility document from `response.document`, then re-read the normalized CanvasDocument before further edits.

## Files, fonts, and privacy

Browser file controls accept `File` or `File[]`, never a filesystem path string. Construct the `File` only from bytes the user authorized. Local images, converted assets, fonts, Lottie files, saved designs, and recovery drafts remain in the browser unless the user explicitly exports or sends them elsewhere.

Generation requests are processed in memory and are not persisted by Glyphfield. Bundled third-party marks and upstream shader/material sources retain their own attribution and ownership.

## Completion rules

A successful request is not sufficient evidence of a finished task.

- After a mutation, re-read source or controls and confirm the new state.
- For a visual task, inspect the authentic canvas.
- For an artifact, confirm the Blob or response body is non-empty and that MIME type, extension, dimensions, and requested format agree.
- For GIF or MP4, inspect multiple frames. For a seamless GIF, verify closure rather than assuming the encoder loop flag creates a visual loop.
- For MP4 with audio, confirm the expected audio track is present. GIF never contains audio.
- If the browser cannot encode MP4, report that limitation and preserve the source. Do not silently substitute GIF.
- If WebGL is unavailable, use a deterministic fallback only when it still satisfies the request.

## Current product model

One active identity supplies name, marks, assets, color roles, type roles, strategy, voice, and defaults to every Studio tool. Studio projects, tabs, and tool drafts persist locally.

Design Lab is the general layer compositor. It combines multiple text, mark, image, shader, sticker, and converter layers; direct manipulation; ordering and grouping; per-layer opacity and blend; Bayer, ASCII, halftone, posterize, and text effects; foreground/background effect colors; independent shader fills; frame-history scrubbing; logarithmic shader size from 0.1× to 10×; surfaces and sticker finishes; saved designs; recovery; and PNG/JPG/GIF/MP4 export.

The shared Shader Library is quality-sorted and used by Design Lab and Animation. Read `/api/materials` for the exact current material list, engine attribution, categories, controls, palettes, and defaults. Never infer a material ID from its display name.

New Design Lab compositions default to Gem Smoke. Saved documents remain authoritative, and authored legacy materials must not be replaced merely because defaults changed.

Animation builds text, mark, and image sequences with per-frame layout, timing, material backgrounds, frame overrides, audio clips, GIF, and MP4. Lottie imports JSON or `.lottie`, supports recoloring, trim/playback, live-material backgrounds, frame PNG, and source download.

Brand identity, Brand elements, Moodboard, Brand book, OpenGraph, Color tokens, Typography, Terminal card, Partnership, Blog, Slides, and Components share the same identity and reusable Studio editor systems. Read `/api/labs` and the relevant docs page for current availability and exact behavior.
